purpose: Separate one-shot archive-provider withdrawal HTTP regression control at the frozen0.7.1 implementation. Additional provider coverage, not a retry/replacement of the immutable14-run packet or any earlier failed capture.
coreBinding: frozen-core.json must bind the exact root-authorized source fingerprint and version after core freeze; no RPC may run before root explicitly confirms freeze.
rules: No live RPC before explicit root freeze authorization; local --check and --bind perform no network requests.
Each case/provider is attempted at most once. Retain all API failures, unavailable measurements, transport failures and budget skips. No substitutions, fallback, retries or provider switching.

Count all RPC response bytes and local HTTP response bytes against the aggregate limit, including a cap-crossing final chunk. Discard oversized content; retain bounded hash and fixed failure metadata.
Use actual product HTTP POST /api/replay via an ephemeral loopback server with recording RPC injection. No shared port5174 dependency.
Every successful RPC retains exact response text/hash and exact JSON request. RPC error envelope bodies are withheld; valid contract-controlled trace errors remain evidence.
Verify frozen source bytes before each attempt and after completion, and compare implementation identity in every HTTP200 response.

Existing original dRPC approval/index failure, archive withdrawal failure, direct-B inconsistency, prospective pilot, and independent seven-pair oracle are immutable; do not manufacture new responses for old call sequences.
These previously inspected development cases are not a held-out accuracy evaluation or security score.
authorization: Root explicitly authorized one separate archive withdrawal run after the original14-run packet completed, at the same frozen source/version, maximum80RPC/8MiBresponse/32MiBtotal/120s, no retries/fallback.
